summary: @servicetitan/line-item-editor preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-prefixed identifiers, object-property indirection typical of javascript-obfuscator output) and downloads the Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts and chmods the bun binary, and then invokes it via execFileSync to run a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated payload using string-array rotation and a ~1000-entry mixed hex/string decoder table with no readable endpoints or strings consistent with the package's stated purpose. The package presents itself as a React TreeList / line-item-editor UI component, which has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime at install time; routing execution through a non-Node runtime evades scanners that trace Node-resolved code. The combination — obfuscated lifecycle script, alternate-runtime fetch, and opaque 727KB payload executed with full user privileges on every install — matches the alternate-runtime-dropper attack pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
